items.prompt: Black to move. Black is already losing material after the knight grab, and the white knight on d4 has no defender. Does taking it with the queen make things better or worse? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: ...Qxd4 scores at least 250 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).
After ...Qxd4 and White's best reply, Black has lost material overall.

hints: Count the pieces that stand between White's queen and the d4 square.
If the bishop on d3 moved away with check, what would the queen on d1 suddenly see?
The bishop can go to b5 with check.
items.explain: The white queen on d1 is blocked by its own bishop on d3, so the knight on d4 looks free. But the bishop can leave with check on b5, which opens the d-file at the same moment. Black must answer the check, and then the white queen takes the black queen. After ...Qxd4 White is about seven pawns ahead, against about four after the quiet ...Bc5 (depth 16).

feedback_by_move.b6d4: This is the capture the trap wants: the d-file opens with check and the queen falls.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's queen has just taken the knight on d4. Find the move that wins it.

claims.statement: Bb5+ is the engine's best move (depth 16).
After Bb5+ and Black's best defence White is at least six pawns up in counting value.

hints: Which of your pieces blocks the queen on d1 from the black queen on d4?
That piece can move with check. Look at the diagonal toward e8.
The bishop goes to b5.
items.explain: The bishop on d3 stands between the white queen and the black queen. Moving it to b5 gives check along the diagonal to e8 and opens the d-file in one move. Black has to meet the check, and then the white queen captures on d4. White ends about a queen ahead at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's queen has just taken on d4. Does White have a check that wins material by force? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Bb5+ wins at least six pawns of counting value (depth 16).

hints: Which check opens the d-file?
The check comes from the bishop.
Bb5+.
items.explain: Black's knight has left c6, so the only blocker is the bishop from c8 on d7, and that does not save the queen. The check opens the d-file and the queen on d4 falls.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's queen has just taken on d4, but this time the black bishop already stands on d7 and White has not castled. Does Bb5 win material by force? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Bb5 scores at least 200 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).

hints: Is Bb5 still a check, with the bishop on d7?
What can the black queen do about the white queen on d1?
Black can trade queens and then take the bishop on b5.
items.explain: With the bishop already on d7, Bb5 is not a check, so Black simply trades queens with ...Qxd1 and then wins the bishop on b5. The discovered attack needs a check that Black cannot answer by taking your queen. At depth 16 Bb5 is at least 2 pawns worse than White's best move.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's queen has just taken on d4, and one black pawn stands on a6 instead of a7. Does White still have a check that wins material by force? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Bb5+ still wins at least six pawns of counting value (depth 16).

hints: Does the pawn on a6 change the d-file or the diagonal to e8?
The a-pawn stands on neither line, but it attacks b5.
The pawn can take the bishop, but then the queen falls.
items.explain: The pawn on a6 attacks b5, and ...axb5 is Black's best reply, but then White takes the queen: a bishop for a queen leaves White still about six pawns ahead, a little less than without the pawn. The edit changes the margin, not the idea.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's pieces point at the king. What does White threaten?

claims.statement: The bishop on d3 attacks h7.
Only the king, on g8, defends h7.

hints: Which white piece looks down a diagonal toward the black king?
The diagonal ends on a pawn that only the king guards.
The bishop takes on h7.
items.explain: The bishop on d3 sees h7, which only the king defends. If Black passed, the bishop would take on h7 with check and the knight on f3 and the queen on g4 would join in.

items.prompt: Black to move. White threatens Bxh7+. Find a good defensive move.

claims.statement: Four moves are within 0.45 pawns of the engine's best: ...Nf5, ...f6, ...f5 and ...Ng6 (depth 16).
After ...f5 a black pawn stands on f5, on the diagonal from d3 to h7.
After ...Nf5 the engine still rates White ahead, between 0.5 and 1.6 pawns (depth 16).

hints: Count the white pieces that aim at h7 or g5, then count the black ones that guard them.
Either put something on the bishop's diagonal from d3 to h7, or cover g5 so a knight check can be taken.
...f5, ...Nf5 and ...Ng6 block the diagonal; ...f6 covers g5.
items.explain: Two ideas defend: put something on the diagonal from d3 to h7 (...f5, ...Nf5, ...Ng6), or take away g5 so the knight's check can be captured (...f6). All of them leave White somewhat better, about 0.9 to 1.3 pawns at depth 16. Moves that change nothing near the king lose quickly. ...Qa5 does not stop the sacrifice, so the engine rates it a little worse.

feedback_by_move.a7a6: A quiet move: Bxh7+ Kxh7 Ng5+ Kg8 Qh5 wins at once.
feedback_by_move.h7h6: Now Bxh6 wins: the pawn on g7 is pinned by the queen and cannot take the bishop.
feedback_by_move.b7b5: A pawn move on the other wing leaves h7 and g5 as they were, so Bxh7+ wins.
feedback_by_move.d8a5: This hits c3 but does not stop Bxh7+; the engine rates it a little worse than the defences that do.

items.prompt: White to move. Black has made a quiet move on the queenside. Find the sacrifice.

claims.statement: Bxh7+ is the engine's best move (depth 16).
After Bxh7+ the engine rates White at least four pawns ahead (depth 16).

hints: Which black pawn is guarded only by the king?
The bishop can take it with check, and a second piece follows.
Bxh7+.
items.explain: Bxh7+ forces the king to take. Ng5+ then comes with check, and Qh5 threatens Qh7 mate. Nothing guards g5, and the black king has no good square. At depth 16 White is more than four pawns ahead.

items.prompt: White to move. Black has played ...a6. Does the bishop sacrifice on h7 win material by force? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: After Bxh7+ the engine rates White at least four pawns ahead (depth 16).

hints: Count the black pieces that guard h7 or g5.
Only the king guards h7, and nothing covers g5.
Bxh7+ Kxh7 Ng5+ and Qh5.
items.explain: Nothing guards g5 and only the king guards h7, so after the king takes, Ng5+ and Qh5 come with decisive threats.

items.prompt: White to move. Black has played ...f6. Does the bishop sacrifice on h7 win material by force? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Bxh7+ scores at least 300 cp worse than the best move (depth 16).
The black pawn on f6 attacks g5, so a knight check there can be captured.

hints: Which square does the knight need for its check?
Who can capture a knight on g5?
The pawn on f6 attacks g5.
items.explain: After Bxh7+ Kxh7 Ng5+ the pawn on f6 simply takes the knight, and White has given a bishop and a knight for a pawn. The sacrifice fails here although the queen still aims at the king.

items.prompt: White to move. Black has played ...b5. Does the bishop sacrifice on h7 win material by force? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: After Bxh7+ the engine rates White at least four pawns ahead (depth 16).

hints: Does the pawn on b5 guard anything near the king?
The b-pawn is on the other side of the board.
Same idea as before: only the king guards h7.
items.explain: The pawn on b5 does not touch h7 or g5, so the sacrifice works as before. A move that changes nothing near the king changes nothing about the idea.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Bxh7+ is the engine's best move (depth 16).

hints: Look at what guards h7 and g5.
The queen left the kingside.
Bxh7+.
items.explain: The queen on b6 guards neither h7 nor g5, so the sacrifice works. At depth 16 it is the engine's best move.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Bxh6 is the engine's best move (depth 16).
After Bxh6 the pawn on g7 has only two legal moves, g6 and g5: it cannot take the bishop on h6 because the queen on g4 pins it to the king.

hints: The pawn on h6 is now the one the king relies on.
Which black pawn cannot recapture on a bishop that lands on h6?
The bishop on c1 takes on h6.
items.explain: The pawn on g7 is pinned to the king by the queen on g4, so ...gxh6 is not allowed; Bxh6 also threatens Bxg7 and Qxg7 mate. This is a different pattern from the h7 sacrifice (a pinned pawn that cannot recapture), not the same idea. At depth 16 it is the engine's best move, well ahead of the next one.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Bxh6 is the engine's best move (depth 16).
Bxh7+ is at least 300 cp worse than the best move here (depth 16).

hints: Check what guards g5 before you sacrifice anything.
The pawn on f6 attacks g5.
Another bishop can go to h6.
items.explain: The pawn on f6 covers g5, so Bxh7+ Kxh7 Ng5+ fxg5 loses two pieces for a pawn. The queen on g4 pins the pawn on g7, so Bxh6 is the strong move instead (depth 16).

feedback_by_move.d3h7: After Bxh7+ Kxh7 Ng5+ the pawn on f6 takes the knight, and White has given two pieces for a pawn.
